svg.title: Scenario: a whole region goes down during trading
svg.text: Scenario: us-east4 goes dark at 11:02 on a Saturday. What keeps taking orders, and what you had to set up beforehand.
The goal is that shoppers see a few slow requests and a handful of retries, not an outage page. RPO for orders is zero because Spanner commits to two regions.
Global external App LB + Cloud Armor + CDN
health checks every 5 s, outlier detection on 5xx
Nothing to fail over by hand at this layer: the load balancer stops sending here on its own.
Runs at about 50% CPU normally, so it absorbs the other half before new nodes arrive.
Writes keep committing with quorum from us-east1 + us-central1. Committed orders are not lost. Expect a short latency bump while leaders move.
Global and multi-region services carry on. Check every regional dependency you have, not just the ones in the diagram.
11:02:00 5xx rate in us-east4 jumps; checkout p95 spikes
11:02:30 health checks fail; LB sends 100% to us-east1
11:02:40 in-flight checkouts retry, same idempotency key
11:03:00 HPA scales pods; Autopilot provisions new nodes
11:03:00 Spanner leaders already serving from us-east1
11:05:00 carts that missed cache rebuild from Spanner
11:06:00 SLO alert closes; error budget burn ~4 minutes
- every region sized to carry 100% (N+1 per region)
- carts and orders live in Spanner, cache is optional
- no region-pinned state in pods or local disks
- PSP allow-list has NAT IPs from both regions
- quarterly game day: drain a region on purpose
